content.comment_body: Hello Expert, I am looking for assistance. I want to log analog data from a [product_name] PLC into an Excel sheet at 20ms intervals.

From my point of view, this isn't feasible. With internal data logging on [product_name], there is a required pause of at least 500ms between log entries. [company_name] offers an Excel log tool, which logs data automatically every second, but this time interval cannot be adjusted.
Is it possible by any means to log data into Excel every 20ms from a [product_name] PLC, or is there a better and more cost-effective alternative? Any support is appreciated. Thank you.

Hi, 1. Collecting data at 20ms intervals doesn't align with technical limits, since analog conversion time on [product_name] is 50ms. The fastest data logging is around 500ms. 2. For 20ms logging, you could use a PC connected to an OPC server to record data at that rate, if you have the necessary expertise. For example, LIBNODAVE is a free OPC server, but other options might exist. Be sure to consider the conversion constraints mentioned above. Hope this clarifies things.

Hi, There are two ways to record data from [product_name] into Excel: 1) Use the built-in datalog feature in [product_name], then export the log file via PC or MSD card (format is CSV). 2) Use the [product_name] Access Tool, which is freely available on the [company_name] website. Differences: [product_name] Datalog works independently from a PC; you need a PC to retrieve the data. The [product_name] Access Tool makes it possible to display and record (CSV format) data directly in Excel while [product_name] operates in RUN mode. You can download the tool or watch tutorials online. Hope this is helpful.

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are aiming to log analog data from a [product_name] PLC into Excel at 20ms intervals, but face technical limitations. The built-in logging functions and analog conversion speeds of the hardware can't meet such fast data collection requirements. Tools provided by [company_name] for Excel integration also enforce minimum intervals higher than the user's target. Users suggest alternative solutions using OPC servers, but even those depend on the device's conversion speed and may require advanced setup. The discussion highlights the need for more flexible and cost-effective data logging options, yet the current product ecosystem does not support rapid logging.
analysis.user_expectations: User wants to log analog data from a [product_name] PLC at 20ms intervals directly into Excel, or find another efficient and affordable way to accomplish high-speed data logging.
